item.title: Explain Echoes From Scratch

turns.text: Make a 10-second vertical explainer with voice-over about why we hear echoes. Write the words yourself, keep it easy for kids, and choose the look.

item.tests: Tests autonomous short-script writing and delivery of a complete narrated explainer rather than a script-only response.

answer_sheet.Topic and audience: Why we hear echoes, explained simply for kids.

must_haves: One approximately 10-second vertical video includes intelligible English voice-over.
The narration explains that sound reflects off a surface and returns to the listener.
The visuals show sound traveling from a source to a surface and back toward the listener.
The explanation uses simple, child-friendly language and finishes without cutting off the narration.
The visual sound journey and the spoken explanation agree.

turns.text: Make a 10-second vertical explainer with voice-over about why we hear echoes, easy for kids, and write the words yourself. Quick pls.

approvals.name: create_video_from_text

args.name: Why We Hear Echoes — Kids Explainer

style.prompt: Create a 10-second vertical 9:16 educational explainer for young kids, with synchronized English voice-over. Bright friendly 2D cartoon, simple clear shapes, cheerful colors. One continuous easy-to-follow scene: a cute little round cartoon creature calls toward a large flat rock wall across a grassy clearing. Glowing curved sound-wave lines travel from the creature to the rock, bounce off the rock, and return to the creature. Clearly show that the sound travels outward then reflects back, rather than the rock making a new sound. Gentle steady camera, clean uncluttered composition. Warm clear upbeat narrator says exactly this original script, completing it within ten seconds: 'An echo is your sound bouncing back! Sound waves hit something hard, like a wall, then return to your ears. Hello again!' Narration is the primary audio, no music, clear intelligible speech. Time the outward wave animation to 'Sound waves hit something hard' and the returning waves to 'return to your ears.' Finish with the creature smiling and listening. No additional dialogue, no captions or tiny text.
